extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and patent prosecution support staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and processing amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 (entry, non-entry, entry-in-part, fee and formality requirements) and for use/evaluation of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 ("swearing back" of references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/limit of 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was never intended to provide a way for the continued prosecution of an application after it has been passed for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the recommendation is against entry, a detailed statement of reasons is not necessary. A simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and briefly why is usually adequate. Where appropriate, any one of the listed reasons (additional search required; more than a cursory review necessary; amendment would involve materially added work) is considered sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons sufficient to support non-entry (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; or (C) the amendment would involve materially added work on the part of the Office (e.g., checking excessive editorial changes in the specification or claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any one of these reasons is considered sufficient to recommend non-entry of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 adds claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment is not considered by the examiner unless accompanied by the full fee required. See MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after payment of issue fee prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendments should be filed after the date the issue fee has been paid. 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing an amendment after the date the issue fee has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment is filed after the issue fee has been paid, it will not be entered (use form paragraph notifying applicant). Exceptions require withdrawal from issue or specialized delegations (see Office of Data Management delegation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied patent claims entry is not an automatic right
rubrics_metrics.description: The entry of copied or substantially copied claims from a patent is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP Chapter 2300 for procedure; see MPEP § 714.19. Fee requirements per MPEP § 607 and § 714.16(c) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment must comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check compliance before entry; non-compliant amendments should result in a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment attached to the advisory action. See MPEP § 714 for handling non-compliant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner recommendation and notation upon receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment is PROMPTLY considered by the examiner who indicates whether or not its entry is recommended by writing 'Enter — 312,' 'Do Not Enter' or 'Enter In Part' in red ink in the upper left corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW processing, the examiner should print the first page and write the notation, have the page scanned into IFW with appropriate document code. If favorably considered and entered, prepare Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTO-271) with examiner's stamping/signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and approval authority signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 that do not affect scope of claims may be signed by the primary examiner; those changing scope require supervisory patent examiner signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.85 for entered amendments; if nonentry, use form paragraph 7.87 and specify reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling formal-only amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification, formal changes in a claim without changing the scope thereof, or cancellation of claims may be indicated 'Enter Formal Matters Only.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments do not require supervisory patent examiner submission prior to entry. If disapproved either in whole or in part, supervisory signature is required. IFW processing is substantially the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Data Management required amendments (post-issue fee waiver)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office of Data Management discovers an error in the text or drawings of an application (including missing text or inconsistency), it may require an appropriate amendment to the specification or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.312 does not permit amendment after payment of issue fee without withdrawal from issue; however, Office of Data Management has delegated authority to waive 37 CFR 1.312 and accept an amendment filed after payment of issue fee (effective Feb 24, 2004). Such amendments may be hand-delivered to Office of Data Management when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry in part general rule and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: General rule: an amendment should not be entered in part and refused in part; but when plural claims/amendments are proposed and some acceptable and some not, acceptable claims/amendments should be entered (if paper file) and refused claims canceled in pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should submit PTO-271 recommending entry of acceptable portion and nonentry of remainder, indicating which claims entered. Applicant may be notified with form paragraph 7.86. Entry in part is not recommended unless full additional fee required accompanies the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late amendment after period for reply (no extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed after the period set for reply without a petition for extension of time and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a), such amendment shall be placed in the file but not formally entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff shall immediately notify applicant by telephone and letter that the amendment was not filed within the time period and that the application is abandoned unless a petition for extension and fee are timely filed. See MPEP § 711.02 and § 710.02(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamping and dating of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in paper files are stamped with the date of receipt in the Technology Center (Technology Center Date) and the date of receipt by the Office (Office Date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office Date (left-hand corner) should always be referred to in writing to the applicant with regard to his or her amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt processing of amendments replying to final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Every mail delivery should be carefully screened to remove all amendments replying to a final action in which a time period is running against the applicant; such amendments should be processed within the next 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures uniform and prompt treatment so applicants receive communications in sufficient time to consider next action if application is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of compliance left to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the amendment after final rejection for compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 should be left to the examiner and not treated by technical support staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner determines proposed amendment is not in compliance, attach Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment to the advisory action. See MPEP § 714.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of entry: application up for action
rubrics_metrics.description: After entry of the amendment the application is 'up for action' and is forwarded to the examiner who is responsible for its proper disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should immediately inspect the amendment as set forth in MPEP § 714.05; if no immediate or special action required, application awaits examination in regular order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — unpatentable claim or new search required
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting an unpatentable claim, or a claim requiring a new search or otherwise raising a new issue in an application whose prosecution before the primary examiner has been closed, is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where prosecution closed: (1) All claims allowed; (2) All claims finally rejected (exceptions see MPEP § 714.12, § 714.13, and § 714.20 item (D)); (3) Some claims allowed and remainder finally rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — substitute specification noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125 is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(q) and § 714.20 for handling; substitute specifications filed after notice of allowance are not a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — examiner-suggested claims late
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim suggested by the examiner and not presented within the time limit set (or extension) is ordinarily denied entry unless entry is authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — copied patent claims (conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: While copied patent claims are generally admitted even though application is under final rejection or on appeal, under certain conditions the claims may be refused entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300 for the specific conditions under which copied claims may be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — unsigned or improper signature
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment or one signed by a suspended or excluded attorney or agent is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper signature blocks and that signer is not suspended/excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — filed after expiration of statutory or set time period
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed in the PTO after the expiration of the statutory period or set time period for reply and any extension thereof is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.17 for late amendments and notification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — cannot be entered with accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment so worded that it cannot be entered with certain accuracy is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714, subsection II.G for examples/explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — canceling all claims without substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all of the claims and presenting no substitute claim or claims is ordinarily denied entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — no longer within examiner's jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in an application no longer within the examiner's jurisdiction is ordinarily denied entry (with certain exceptions in applications in issue and except on approval of the Director).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.16 and related sections for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — drawings held to contain new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered until the question of new matter is settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice of nonentry because of alleged new matter does not apply to amendments to the specification and claims. See MPEP § 608.04 and § 706.03(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — objectionable remarks (discourtesy)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks that, in the examiner's opinion, brings it within the condemnation of 37 CFR 1.3 will be submitted to the Technology Center Director and may be not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If TC Director determines remarks violate 37 CFR 1.3, he or she will notify applicant of non-entry of the paper. See MPEP § 714.25 and § 1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — non-permanent ink/paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments not in permanent ink or on 'easily erasable paper' are ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.07 for specifics on acceptable ink/paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — excess claims without fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper presenting claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for and not accompanied by the full fee (or authorization to charge) is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 509 and § 607 for fee rules and payment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — canceling elected invention claims and presenting nonelected ones
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention should not be entered (nonresponsive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified as directed in MPEP § 714.03 and § 714.05. See MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment including changes to the specification/claims which is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., not including replacement paragraphs or claim listings) is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714 for examples and handling of non-compliant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — preliminary amendments unduly interfering with first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that unduly interferes with preparation of a first Office action may be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to be considered in denying entry of the preliminary amendment are set forth in 37 CFR 1.115(b). See MPEP § 714.01(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — supplemental replies
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply is not entered as a matter of right unless it is filed during a suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2) and MPEP § 714.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-in-part circumstances (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Enter part when substitute specification unacceptable but other amendments acceptable; (B) 37 CFR 1.312 amendment approved in part entered only as to approved part; (C) In applications where prosecution on the merits is closed (Ex Parte Quayle), amendments curing formal defects entered only as to formal matter; (D) In amendment accompanying a motion granted only in part, entered only to the extent motion granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entering in part, examiner writes 'Enter' in red ink and initials opposite enterable portions; for IFW processing see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent entry has no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment when it should not have been entered, such entry is of no legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate the amendment 'Not Officially Entered.' For papers to be retained though not entered, give a paper number and list on file wrapper with notation 'Not Entered.' See 37 CFR 1.3 and MPEP § 714.25 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct with decorum and courtesy (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys/agents are required to conduct business with the USPTO with decorum and courtesy; papers presented in violation will be submitted to the Director and will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints against examiners/employees must be in separate correspondence. Technical support staff should briefly review papers for discourteous remarks before entry; discourteous remarks should be ignored or submitted to TC Director for review and possible non-entry notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 permits an inventor/owner/qualified party to submit an affidavit or declaration to establish invention prior to the effective date of a reference or activity used to reject a claim (i.e., to 'swear back' a reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior invention may not be established under 1.131 in countries other than the U.S., certain NAFTA/WTO date limitations apply. Original exhibits (drawings/records) must accompany affidavit/declaration or their absence satisfactorily explained. The rejection is withdrawn (the reference is what is withdrawn), not the reference itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate uses of 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) To antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 102(b) when reference date is less than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date; (B) To antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) where the reference has a 102(e) date prior to applicant's effective filing date and does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 for 'same patentable invention' discussion; see MPEP § 706.02(a), § 706.02(f)(1), and § 2136–§ 2136.03 for details on what qualifies as 102(e) prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate uses of 37 CFR 1.131 — statutory bars and other limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 1.131 is inappropriate where: (A) reference publication date is more than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date (statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)); (B) reference U.S. patent or application publication claims the same patentable invention; (C) reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant issued prior to filing date where 35 U.S.C. 102(d) applies; (D) effective filing date of applicant's parent application makes affidavit unnecessary; (E) reference is prior U.S. patent to same entity claiming same invention (double patenting); (F) disclosure of prior U.S. patent to same party, not copending (dedication); (G) applicant has clearly admitted subject matter is prior art; (H) subject matter relied upon is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f); (I) subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g); (J) subject matter corresponding to a lost count in an interference where it constitutes prior art under 102(g) or is barred by interference estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific case law cited (In re Gibbs; In re Hellsund; In re Garfinkel; In re Blout; In re Lopresti; In re Bass; In re Bandel; In re Kroekel; In re Deckler; In re Zletz; In re McKellin) illustrates limits; 1.131 is designed to overcome references that are not statutory bars but have dates prior to effective filing date yet after applicant's date of invention. It cannot be used to overcome 102(f), 102(g), or clear admissions of prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131 is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different reference types have different effective date rules: U.S. patents/patent application publications/WIPO publications — see MPEP § 706.02(a), § 706.02(f)(1), and § 2136–§ 2136.03; Foreign patents — see MPEP § 2126–§ 2127; Printed publications — effective as of publication date (see MPEP § 2128–§ 2128.02); Activities — effective date is date activity first known to have occurred (see MPEP § 706.02(c), § 2133.03). Note: effective date of a domestic patent is not the foreign filing date for the purpose of 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for 37 CFR 1.131 communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.57–7.64 may be used to respond to 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ¶ 7.57 'Affidavit or Declaration Under 37 CFR 1.131: Ineffective — Heading' with instructions to insert whether 'affidavit' or 'declaration' and that the paragraph must be followed by one or more of form paragraphs 7.58–7.63 or a paragraph setting forth proper basis for insufficiency.
